before: A nested grid normally chooses its own tracks. Its rows can differ from nearby cards even when their outer boxes align.
subgrid lets a nested grid use the parent grid’s tracks along the selected axis. It does not create a new independent row-sizing system for that axis.
For row sharing, a card must span the parent rows it will use. grid-row: span 2 makes the card cover two rows.
When one title needs more height, the shared title row can make room for it. Both cards’ body rows then begin at the same parent row boundary.
The supplied board has two cards. The first title is44px tall and the second is20px tall; each body is24px tall. Their different title sizes are deliberate.
Change the cards to use subgrid rows, keeping their two-row span. Do not hide, truncate, or force both titles to one fixed height to fake alignment.
This exercise shares rows only. Column subgrid is a separate choice; adding subgrid does not automatically share both axes.
after: A card can have a grid inside it. Usually, that inner grid chooses its own row sizes. This can make text in nearby cards start at different heights.
A subgrid shares rows or columns with its parent grid. Here, each card shares the parent's rows.
Each card needs to cover the rows it shares. `grid-row: span 2` makes it cover two rows: one for the title and one for the body text.
If one title is taller, the shared title row can grow to fit it. The body text in both cards still starts at the same row edge.
The first supplied title is 44 pixels tall. The second is 20 pixels tall. Their different heights help you see what sharing rows does.
Keep both titles fully visible and keep their different heights. Let the shared rows line up the body text.
This rule shares rows only. Sharing columns would need its own setting.

before.question: One card’s title grows taller while neighboring cards share its parent title/body rows through subgrid. What should happen to the body starting positions?
choices: Each card must keep an unrelated body position.
The shorter card must hide its title.
The shared track can grow so the bodies still start on the same row boundary.
before.explanation: The cards use shared parent rows rather than independently choosing title-row heights.

after.question: One title gets taller. What happens when both cards share the title and body rows?
choices: Each body must start at a different height
The shorter title must be hidden
The shared row can grow, keeping the bodies lined up
after.explanation: Both cards use the same row edges, so their bodies can stay lined up.
